update_log: Baseline initialization of high-frequency scientific discoveries and technological inventions for Miscellaneous Static GK.

physics_and_chemistry.key_fact: Discovered using cathode ray tubes. Thomson was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1906.
Though Eugen Goldstein discovered canal rays (positive ions) earlier, Rutherford is credited with naming and formally discovering the proton.
Discovered that this particle had a mass similar to a proton but no electrical charge. Won the Nobel Prize in 1935.
Accidentally discovered while experimenting with cathode rays. Earned the first-ever Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.
Discovered spontaneously emitted radiation from uranium salts. Later expanded upon by Marie and Pierre Curie.
Organized elements by atomic mass and brilliantly left gaps for undiscovered elements, predicting their properties.

medical_and_biology.key_fact: The world's first widely effective antibiotic, discovered accidentally from a mold called Penicillium notatum.
The world's first vaccine. Jenner used cowpox material to create immunity to smallpox.
Salk developed the first safe and effective injectable vaccine. Sabin later developed the oral drop vaccine used globally today.
Made blood transfusions safe by classifying human blood into A, B, AB, and O groups.
Identified the double-helix structure of DNA, relying heavily on X-ray diffraction images taken by Rosalind Franklin.

technology_and_everyday_inventions.key_fact: Awarded the first US patent for the telephone. His first words were 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you'.
Did not invent the first electric light, but created the first commercially practical, long-lasting incandescent bulb.
Demonstrated the world's first working mechanical television system.
Achieved the first successful, sustained, and controlled heavier-than-air powered flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
Invented while working at CERN to help scientists share data globally. He created the first web browser and web server.
